rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for the building material in everyday Hong Kong Cantonese.

example.english: This wall is made of concrete.
example.jyutping: ni1 fuk1 coeng4 hai6 jung6 sek6 si2 zing2 ge3

rows.note: Use this technical or written term in construction, engineering, and formal descriptions.

example.english: The engineer said this wall needs to be built with concrete.
example.traditional: 工程師話呢幅牆要用混凝土建造。
example.jyutping: gung1 cing4 si1 waa6 ni1 fuk1 coeng4 jiu3 jung6 wan6 jing4 tou2 gin3 zou6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something specific or tangible rather than abstract.

example.english: I want some concrete examples, not just general principles.
example.traditional: 我想要啲具體例子，唔好淨係講大道理。
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 jiu3 di1 geoi6 tai2 lai6 zi2 m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 gong2 daai6 dou6 lei5

rows.note: Use this colloquial noun-modifying construction for something made of concrete, such as a concrete building or floor.

example.english: This concrete building can last for decades.
example.traditional: 呢幢石屎樓起碼可以捱幾十年。
example.jyutping: ni1 zong6 sek6 si2 lau4 hei2 maa5 ho2 ji5 ngaai4 gei2 sap6 nin4

rows.note: Use this when concrete means real or actual and tangibility is not the focus.

example.english: I want concrete information, not estimates.
example.traditional: 我想要真實嘅資料，唔係估計。
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 jiu3 zan1 sat6 ge3 zi1 liu6 m4 hai6 gu2 gai3
